forecasts.question: Will Iran and Oman jointly announce a formal Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor arrangement before EOD 2026-08-08?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from initial 0.38 proposal to 0.35. Araghchi's 'final stages' language (IRNA/Al Jazeera, August 2) and the July 28-29 formal proposal exchange provide genuine evidence of near-term possibility. Core disagreement on Iran's transit service-fee — framed as legitimate maritime security compensation by Tehran, rejected as an illegal toll by Washington — remains unresolved. The 4-day window and US political resistance to any framework that formalizes IRGC control over Hormuz access reduce probability below the initial proposal. US non-acceptance does not affect resolution; Iranian and Omani announcement alone resolves this forecast.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if both Iran's Foreign Ministry and Oman's Foreign Ministry publicly announce, or a formal joint communiqué is issued, confirming a Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor arrangement that specifies at minimum (a) the corridor route or geographic parameters, and (b) either a fee structure or a confirmed no-fee arrangement, before EOD 2026-08-08.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IRNA or Oman News Agency (ONA) announcing the framework, confirmed by one TIER1 source (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera). Either government's unilateral announcement independently confirmed by TIER1 also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Araghchi or Omani FM stating talks are in 'final stages' or 'nearing conclusion' without a formal announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A framework that leaves fee structure, route, or effective date as TBD = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. US government acceptance or opposition does NOT affect resolution — this forecast measures the Iran-Oman bilateral announcement only.

forecasts.question: Will the United States military conduct confirmed new strikes against targets on Iranian soil before EOD 2026-08-11?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from initial 0.27 proposal to 0.24. Trump threatened a 'multi-day air campaign — the biggest since World War II' against Iran on August 1, then canceled the same evening citing 'the perimeters of a deal' — a pattern of threat-and-retract consistent with prior behavior. Iran killed two US service members in Jordan on July 18-19 (CNN/Britannica), LNG tanker struck August 1, and Trump issued 'last chance' language August 3. The canceled campaign is the decisive evidence of a decision threshold that has not yet been crossed despite cumulative provocation. p=0.24 reflects the residual escalation risk within 7 days given active military exchanges and the lack of a diplomatic off-ramp.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Pentagon or CENTCOM confirms airstrikes, missile strikes, or special-operations raids conducted by US forces against targets located within Iran's internationally recognized land borders before EOD 2026-08-11. Strikes against Iranian naval vessels or IRGC-directed proxies in Iraq, Syria, Yemen, or at sea do NOT qualify.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump public threat or warning without confirmed execution = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Strikes against Iranian proxies in third countries do not count. If target location on Iranian soil is disputed by both sides, default to NO. US strikes against Iranian vessels at sea = NO.

forecasts.question: Will a formal US-Iran negotiating session — direct or mediated by a named state mediator — be confirmed by both parties before EOD 2026-08-18?

Trump's concurrent assertion that talks were 'set to begin Monday' and a deal was 'imminent' creates genuine uncertainty but reflects a repeated pattern of premature US-side optimism not matched by Iranian confirmation. The Oman-Iran Hormuz corridor track does not constitute a US-Iran negotiating session (the US is not a party). Residual p=0.26 reflects: a 14-day window provides more runway than the Oman track; Trump has historically convened sessions despite Iranian public denials; back-channel communications through Pakistan and Qatar appear ongoing.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Reuters or AP reports — with named spokespeople or officials from both the US and Iran — that a face-to-face negotiating session (direct, or third-country mediated by Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, or another named state) was held between named US and Iranian government principals or envoys before EOD 2026-08-18. forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP carrying confirmation from both a named US government representative (State Dept, NSA, CENTCOM, or designated envoy) AND a named Iranian government representative (MFA official or designated envoy). One-sided confirmation from the US side alone = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump assertion without Iranian MFA confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Oman-Iran bilateral session without US participation = does NOT count. Written message exchanges or intermediary-relayed communications without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. 'Talks about talks' or preparatory meetings without substantive negotiation do NOT count.

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping transits through the Strait of Hormuz reach ≥30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average, IMF PortWatch) before EOD 2026-09-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from initial 0.22 proposal to 0.20. Current baseline is approximately 5-10 non-Western vessels per day following the July 7 MOU breakdown, down from the June-early July partial recovery of ~25/day under the MOU. Lloyd's List Intelligence recorded zero Western-allied transits since May 4. The IRGC Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime (up to $2M per vessel) creates a structural barrier to recovery. Recovery to 30/day (7-day average) requires at minimum the Oman corridor (F1) to become operative, partial P&I insurance reinstatement, and continued absence of new Iranian interdiction activity — a sequence of three dependencies. IMF PortWatch 7-day average is the sole measurement instrument per hygiene framework.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch records a 7-day rolling average of ≥30 commercial vessel transits per day through the Strait of Hormuz in any consecutive 7-day window with the final day falling before EOD 2026-09-07.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch public dashboard (portwatch.imf.org) as primary source. If PortWatch is temporarily unavailable, Lloyd's List Intelligence or Bloomberg shipping-data report may substitute; flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict by >20%. Single-day figures do not resolve; the full 7-day rolling average is required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Single-day spikes above 30 without a qualifying 7-day rolling average = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Naval-escorted convoys count toward transit total. If PortWatch data is unavailable for more than 3 consecutive days within the window, extend horizon by equivalent days and flag AMBIGUOUS until data restored.

forecasts.question: Will Iran agree to a verified freeze or transfer of its highly enriched uranium (≥60% enriched) stockpile as part of a binding framework before EOD 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from initial 0.22 proposal to 0.13. The Islamabad MOU has collapsed (July 7-10); no US-Iran negotiating session is confirmed or planned as of August 3; Iran's Foreign Ministry denied all negotiations on August 3. IAEA Day 157 (August 3) data confirms 440.9 kg of UF6 enriched to 60% remains in-country, sufficient for approximately 10 devices if further enriched — no indication of transfer or verified freeze discussions. A binding HEU framework requires resumed talks, agreed verification mechanism, IAEA supervision protocol, and political will from a Supreme Leader (Mojtaba Khamenei, installed March 8) not seen in public since his appointment. The 84-day window provides meaningful runway; Trump's stated goal of 'ultimately the denuclearization of Iran' (August 2-3) keeps this on the US agenda. p=0.13 reflects the low probability under current conflict baseline.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran officially agrees — in a written document cosigned or formally witnessed by the IAEA or a named state guarantor — to either (a) a verified freeze of its ≥60% enriched UF6 stockpile at or below the August 4, 2026 IAEA-confirmed level, with continuous IAEA monitoring, or (b) transfer of its ≥60% enriched UF6 stockpile to a named third country, before EOD 2026-10-27.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA Director General's written report or official press statement confirming the arrangement as primary source, plus Reuters/AP confirmation. IRNA (Iran state media) acknowledging the agreement alongside IAEA confirmation also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Verbal commitment to future freeze without a signed, witnessed document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Framework reducing new enrichment rates but not addressing the existing stockpile = does NOT count. Provisional or temporary halt without IAEA continuous monitoring = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump or Iranian FM assertion of 'agreement in principle' without IAEA confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a right-wing bloc led by Netanyahu's Likud win ≥61 Knesset seats in Israel's October 27, 2026 legislative election?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from initial 0.28 proposal to 0.22. Netanyahu's bloc polls at approximately 48 seats — the lowest recorded figure for his coalition — against the 61-seat majority threshold in the 120-member Knesset; Likud individually polls at 22-25 seats (Haaretz, July 17). The 13-seat gap between current polling and the majority threshold is substantial. Israeli elections historically see 8-12 seat campaign swings, and wartime incumbency and security narratives could benefit Netanyahu's bloc. However, reaching 61 from 48 requires a swing at the upper end of historical variance, and the direction of swing under the current polling environment — with Netanyahu's bloc at its recorded low — is uncertain. Resolution date set at 2026-11-15 to allow for certified final count; election day is October 27.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, in the Israeli Knesset election of October 27, 2026, the combined certified seat total of all right-wing parties publicly committing to support a Netanyahu-led government reaches ≥61 seats in the final certified results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee before EOD 2026-11-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official certified results, carried by Reuters/AP/Times of Israel/Haaretz. Exit polls alone do not resolve; certified count required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary exit polls or election-night projections without certified final count = AMBIGUOUS pending certification. If recount is in progress at EOD 2026-11-15, extend horizon by 7 days and maintain OPEN-AMBIGUOUS status. If no Netanyahu-led government is attempted despite ≥61 right-wing seats, resolve YES based on seat count alone. Parties committing to a non-Netanyahu right-wing PM do not count toward the 61.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: 55-day catch-up update: p reduced from 0.35 to 0.06. The Knesset voted 62-0 to dissolve on July 17 (Times of Israel/JNS), setting election for October 27. This was an orderly, consensual dissolution in which the coalition retained its majority until the moment of dissolution; it does NOT constitute a majority loss. The coalition completed a full four-year term — the first in decades for an Israeli government per reporting. Both YES resolution criteria are now structurally foreclosed: (a) no Knesset chamber exists to register a majority-loss vote (Knesset is dissolved), and (b) the election is fixed at October 27 itself, which is NOT 'earlier than' October 27. Netanyahu holds caretaker authority through election day; the government is constitutionally stable in the caretaker period. Both indicators are CONTRADICTED. p=0.06 reserved for extraordinary constitutional scenarios (e.g., emergency mechanism setting an earlier election date) for which no current evidence exists. Most likely resolution: NO at the October 27 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (below 61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact through dissolution.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve. Caretaker PM operation during normal election campaign does NOT constitute loss of majority.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas. Orderly end-of-term dissolution with election fixed at or after Oct 27 = RESOLVE-NO at horizon.
